interactions.flavorLineOne:
"Starhorse was pleased with your recent performance," Xûr says. "You were a most satisfactory contestant."

"If you entertain the horse further—if you can set its astral mane flowing with beautiful starlight—it will allow me to give you more gifts claimed from the paraversal jetsam. It is an honor to be able to serve such a magnificent being, is it not?"

The sound of clopping hooves plays through your mind, and you feel as though you are being nuzzled on a molecular, almost mathematical level.

"May the many challenges and rewards of Eternity reveal themselves to you," Xûr says.

headerDisplayProperties.name: To the Daring Go the Spoils

interactions.flavorLineOne: Xûr doesn't have much to call his own, but he'll always have your gift. Until he eats them. If he does eat.

"My hands do not belong to me," says Xûr, almost to himself.

"They are attached to this body, and yet their actions are those of the Nine, or perhaps the impossible horse…"

His hooded visage turns toward you. You can see the vague suggestion of his eyes.

"My hands have made you a key, Guardian. They engraved words upon it, but they did not permit me to see what they were. The message was not for me."

For a moment, Xûr looks at the bizarre splendor around him. "Though I stand amongst treasures, I am but a conduit. They belong to you."

"Tell me, Guardian," he says softly, "is it not wonderful to be loved so deeply?"

Then there is a shift in his countenance, reality shimmers around him, and Xûr falls silent once more.

Xûr bows humbly as you approach.

"I apologize for abducting you earlier," he says, "but I was not given a choice. It was the will of the great Starhorse."

Xûr gestures grandly, and you sense the aspect of a horse teasing at the edges of your mind.

"As you can see, the horse has entrusted me with treasures from across the paraverse—realities different from our own. To gaze upon such impossible objects would rend the minds of most, but you…"

Xûr nods deeply and speaks with hushed reverence: "You have been chosen by the horse."

A neigh echoes through your mind.

"I have been told to reward your triumphs in the Dares of Eternity, and I must obey. Go, compete, and claim these fantastic treasures as your own."

headerDisplayProperties.name: To the Daring Go the Spoils

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"How did you find tonight's Dares of Eternity, contestant? Was my performance of the ancient ritual of 'hosting' to your satisfaction?"

Xûr gazes at the shifting aspect of Starhorse. "It pleases the horse when I speak those sacred words…"

He hesitates. "…though I do not understand all that the horse asks of me. But there is much I do not understand."

He composes himself. "I keep another mystery, Guardian. I know of a key that will lead you to great paraversal riches. The astral steed will allow me to create this key for you if you dedicate yourself to its whims, as I have."

Xûr does not wait for you to respond. "Bring Strange Coins back to the impossible horse. This is the first step… and something tells me we are just getting started."

As you enter his chamber, Xûr greets you with obvious excitement.

"Ah, you have already claimed the access card I plucked from a cleft in the paraversal crush," he says. "It guided me to a weapon part, which I have held for you."

"The omniscient steed believes this treasure would be a fitting reward for your complete mastery of the Dares of Eternity. Do so, and this mechanism shall be yours."

Xûr pauses. "Guardian," he begins, then wrings his hands.

He takes a breath. "These Dares of Eternity are not truly real. They are a paraversal remainder, and when the impossible horse leaves us and the realities realign, they will disappear forever. It will be as though they never existed."

"My memories of hosting, of the time I spent with you… they will disappear along with the Dares." 

"Please, keep the treasures of this place close, so that you are reminded of the time we shared. Remember for me when I cannot."

Xûr's expression does not change, but you feel an aura of deep melancholy emanating from him… yet mixed with that sadness, there is fierce pride.

"Guardian?" Xûr adds.

"Thank you for playing."

"Greetings, Guardian," Xûr says slowly as you arrive in his impossible space. "I have knowledge of a matter that was once lost, but is now prepared to come home."

The expression on his face is serene. "There is comfort in returning matter to its correct place, is there not?"

Before you can answer, he opens his palm. A swirling of particles, fine as iron filings, form a familiar face: Shaw Han. "This legend begins where all new legends do: the Cosmodrome," Xûr says. "Where it ends is up to you."

"The trumpet sounds again, Guardian," he whispers, and that is all.
